concept.name: Helm Chart Releases

relationships.description: Connects Helm Chart Releases to canary deployments in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Helm packages Kubernetes manifests into versioned charts and tracks each deployment as an immutable, numbered release revision stored in-cluster for repeatable upgrades and rollbacks.
spark.keyTakeaway: Helm's value lies in atomic, revision-tracked releases (`--atomic --wait`) and parameterized reuse—treat rendered manifests as immutable build outputs and never mix manual `kubectl edit` into Helm-managed resources.

concept.whyItMatters: Deploying a microservice to Kubernetes touches 6–15 YAML objects (`Deployment`, `Service`, `Ingress`, `HPA`, `ServiceAccount`, `ConfigMap`, `PodDisruptionBudget`). Copy-pasting YAML across dev, staging, and prod drifts immediately. Helm renders Go templates against layered `values.yaml` overrides, applies them in dependency order, waits for readiness probes, and stores compressed release snapshots (`sh.helm.release.v1.<name>.v<N>`) so a broken deploy can roll back in one command.
whenToUse: Packaging third-party infrastructure (ingress-nginx, Prometheus, cert-manager, Kafka operators) distributed as OCI or HTTP Helm repositories.
Standardizing internal microservice deployments across dozens of teams via a shared library or golden base chart.
Needing one-command atomic upgrades (`helm upgrade --install --atomic`) with pre/post-upgrade hooks (e.g., DB schema migrations) and instant revision rollback.
whenNotToUse: Simple, single-team apps with 2–3 static manifests where plain Kustomize overlays avoid Go-template string-escaping headaches.
GitOps pipelines where Argo CD or Flux must see every rendered Kubernetes resource in Git before applying—use `helm template` in CI rather than running `helm upgrade` imperatively.
Managing stateful multi-step day-2 operations (failover, backup/restore, shard rebalancing) better handled by a custom Kubernetes Operator.
keyPoints: `Chart.yaml` separates the chart's own SemVer `version` (template changes) from `appVersion` (the container image tag deployed).
Values merge left-to-right with increasing precedence: chart `values.yaml` < parent chart values < `-f env.yaml` (later files win) < `--set` / `--set-string` flags.
Helm v3 stores each release revision as a gzipped, base64-encoded JSON blob inside a Kubernetes `Secret` (`sh.helm.release.v1.<release>.v<rev>`) in the release namespace.
Lifecycle hooks (`pre-install`, `post-upgrade`, `pre-rollback`) run Kubernetes `Job`s or `Pod`s outside normal release ownership unless given `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy`.
Helm v3.8+ supports OCI registries (`oci://ghcr.io/org/chart`) natively, unifying container image and chart signing/distribution via Cosign and SBOMs.

examples.title: Atomic canary-safe upgrade with DB migration hook
examples.scenario: A payments API rolls out `v2.4.0` requiring an additive PostgreSQL migration before new pods start serving traffic.
examples.outcome: A `Job` annotated with `helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade` and `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded` runs the migration first. `helm upgrade payments oci://registry/payments --version 2.4.0 --atomic --wait --timeout 5m` pauses; if the new `Deployment` pods fail readiness within 5 minutes, Helm automatically rolls back to revision `v11`.

examples.title: Avoiding 1 MiB etcd Secret limit on large umbrella charts
examples.scenario: A platform team bundles 18 microservices and large ConfigMaps into a single umbrella chart, causing `helm upgrade` to fail with `Secret "sh.helm.release.v1.core.v42" is invalid: data: Too long: must have at most 1048576 bytes`.
examples.outcome: They split the umbrella into per-service releases, set `--history-max 10` to prune old revisions, and move multi-megabyte static assets out of `ConfigMap` templates.

tradeOffs.pro: Helm supports loops, conditionals, helper partials (`_helpers.tpl`), and typed schema validation (`values.schema.json`).
tradeOffs.con: Whitespace-sensitive YAML inside Go templates (`{{- ... | nindent 8 }}`) is hard to read and debug compared to Kustomize's strategic-merge patches.

tradeOffs.pro: `helm upgrade --atomic` handles hooks, readiness waits, and automatic rollback directly from CI.
tradeOffs.con: CI pipelines need cluster kubeconfig access, and drift from manual `kubectl` edits goes unnoticed unless a GitOps controller reconciles continuously.

tradeOffs.pro: One command stands up an entire environment with shared global values.
tradeOffs.con: Couples failure domains: one broken subchart blocks the whole release and risks hitting Kubernetes' 1 MiB etcd Secret size limit.

failureModes.name: Stuck `pending-upgrade` release lock
failureModes.description: A CI runner is killed mid-deploy, leaving the latest Secret in `status: pending-upgrade`. Every subsequent `helm upgrade` fails with `another operation (install/upgrade/rollback) is in progress`.
failureModes.mitigation: Run `helm rollback <release> <last-deployed-rev>` (or `helm history` to verify the last `deployed` revision) rather than deleting the Secret manually.

failureModes.name: Implicit type coercion with `--set`
failureModes.description: Passing `--set image.tag=123456` or `--set app.id=1e5` makes Helm parse the value as a float64 (`1.23456e+05`), breaking container image pulls or pod env vars.
failureModes.mitigation: Always use `--set-string`, quote values in `-f values.yaml`, and enforce types with `values.schema.json`.

failureModes.name: Orphaned hook Jobs blocking re-deploys
failureModes.description: A `pre-upgrade` Job without `hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation` already exists on the second upgrade, failing with `jobs.batch "migrate" already exists`.
failureModes.mitigation: Include `"helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded` on all hook resources and give Jobs immutable or revision-suffixed names (`{{ .Release.Revision }}`).

failureModes.name: Manual `kubectl edit` drift overwritten silently
failureModes.description: An on-call engineer patches `replicas: 10` via `kubectl scale`, and the next `helm upgrade` resets `replicas` back to `3` from `values.yaml`.
failureModes.mitigation: Run `helm diff upgrade` in CI before applying, omit `replicas` from the Deployment template when an HPA manages scaling, and restrict production `kubectl` write RBAC.

commonMistakes: Leaving `--history-max` at `10` or unlimited without checking Secret count, or conversely setting it to `0` (infinite) and bloating etcd.
Hardcoding `replicas` inside `Deployment` when a `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` is enabled, causing Helm upgrades to reset autoscaled replica counts.
Using `helm upgrade --force` routinely—`--force` deletes and recreates resources (causing downtime on `Service` or `PVC` immutability errors) instead of patching.
Modifying `values.yaml` without running `helm lint` and `helm template` in CI, letting broken indentation reach the cluster.
Storing plaintext database passwords in `values.yaml` inside Git instead of referencing External Secrets / Sealed Secrets.

sections.content:
## The idea

Helm is a **package manager and release state machine** for Kubernetes. A **chart** is a directory (or `.tgz` / OCI artifact) containing `Chart.yaml` metadata, `values.yaml` defaults, optional `values.schema.json`, and Go `text/template` files under `templates/`.

When you run `helm upgrade --install`, Helm does not just pipe YAML to `kubectl apply`. It merges values, renders templates deterministically, diffs the desired manifests against the **previous release revision** stored in-cluster, computes a 3-way strategic merge patch, executes ordered lifecycle hooks, waits for workload readiness, and writes a new immutable revision record (`v1`, `v2`, `v3`...).

## Concrete walkthrough

Trace `helm upgrade --install orders oci://ghcr.io/acme/orders --version 1.8.2 -f prod.yaml --set-string image.tag=a3f9c12 --atomic --wait --timeout 5m`:

1. **Pull & Validate**: Helm pulls the OCI chart artifact, verifies its `values.schema.json` against the merged values (`values.yaml` + `prod.yaml` + `--set-string`), and renders `templates/*.yaml` locally.
2. **Lock Revision (`pending-upgrade`)**: Helm reads `sh.helm.release.v1.orders.v7` from the target namespace, computes the diff, and writes `v8` with `status: pending-upgrade`.
3. **Pre-Upgrade Hooks**: Any resource tagged `helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade` (sorted by `helm.sh/hook-weight`, e.g., `-5` before `0`) is created and watched until completion.
4. **Apply & Wait**: Helm applies updated `ConfigMap`, `Service`, and `Deployment` manifests. With `--wait`, it polls the Kubernetes API until all new `Deployment` pods pass `readinessProbe`.
5. **Commit or Atomic Rollback**: If all pods become Ready within `5m`, Helm updates `v8` to `status: deployed` and marks `v7` as `superseded`. If a pod `CrashLoopBackOff`s past `5m`, `--atomic` automatically triggers a rollback to `v7` and exits non-zero in CI.

data.title: Helm atomic upgrade and revision state machine

edges.label: Pull chart + verify
edges.title: Fetch immutable chart
edges.description: Pulls versioned chart archive from OCI registry and validates `values.schema.json`.

edges.label: Read v7 + write v8 (pending)
edges.title: Create pending revision
edges.description: Diffs rendered manifests against `v7` and persists `v8` as `pending-upgrade`.

edges.label: Run pre-upgrade hooks
edges.title: Execute ordered hooks
edges.description: Runs `pre-upgrade` Jobs (e.g., DB migrations) sorted by `hook-weight`.

edges.label: Apply manifests + --wait
edges.title: Patch workloads & poll readiness
edges.description: Applies `Deployment`/`Service` patches and waits up to `--timeout` for Ready pods.

edges.label: Commit deployed / rollback
edges.title: Finalize revision state
edges.description: Marks `v8` `deployed` (and `v7` `superseded`), or `--atomic` reverts to `v7` on failure.

data.caption: Helm tracks every release revision in-cluster as a compressed Secret, enabling deterministic 3-way diffs and automatic rollback on failed readiness checks.

sections.content:
## Values precedence, hooks & checksum annotations

A classic Kubernetes pitfall occurs when you update a `ConfigMap`, run `helm upgrade`, and existing pods keep running with stale configuration because the `Deployment` pod spec didn't change. Helm solves this cleanly via a **template checksum annotation**:

```yaml
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checksum/config: {{ include (print $.Template.BasePath "/configmap.yaml") . | sha256sum }}
```

Whenever `configmap.yaml` renders differently, the `checksum/config` SHA-256 changes, triggering a rolling restart of the `Deployment`. Similarly, `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` protects stateful resources (like `PersistentVolumeClaim`s or `Namespace`s) from deletion during `helm uninstall`.

## Kubernetes packaging & deployment comparison

| Aspect | Helm (`helm upgrade`) | Kustomize (`kubectl apply -k`) | GitOps + Helm (Argo CD) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Parameterization** | Go templates + `values.yaml` + JSON Schema | Overlay patches (`patchesStrategicMerge`) | Helm `values` rendered by controller |
| **Revision tracking** | In-cluster Secrets (`v1`, `v2`, ...) | None natively (relies on Git history) | Git commit SHA + Argo sync history |
| **Lifecycle hooks** | Native (`pre-upgrade`, `post-install`) | None (external CI scripts) | Maps Helm hooks to Argo Sync Waves |
| **Drift detection** | Only on `helm diff` / next upgrade | Only on `kubectl diff` | Continuous reconciliation loop |
| **Atomic rollback** | Built-in `--atomic --wait` | Manual `git revert` + re-apply | Automated self-heal / manual rollback |

## Failure modes

- **1 MiB Secret overflow**: Storing large files or 50+ historical revisions in `sh.helm.release.v1.*` hits etcd's 1 MiB object limit. Cap `--history-max 10` and keep large payloads in object storage.
- **Helm + Argo CD hook impedance mismatch**: If you use Argo CD to deploy Helm charts, Argo runs `helm template` and translates `helm.sh/hook` into `argocd.argoproj.io/hook`, but `pre-rollback` hooks are not executed by Argo CD.
- **Race conditions on CRDs**: Helm's `crds/` directory installs CRDs once on `helm install` and **never upgrades or deletes them** on `helm upgrade` to avoid wiping custom resources. Manage CRD upgrades in a dedicated chart or pre-sync step.
- **Non-deterministic `lookup` or `randAlphaNum` functions**: Using `randAlphaNum` inside a `Secret` template regenerates a new password on *every* `helm upgrade`, breaking running apps. Use `lookup` to preserve existing values or manage secrets externally.

## Chart testing, OCI distribution & security

Treat charts like application code. Run `helm lint --strict`, `helm template` piped into `kubeconform` (verifying against the target Kubernetes API version, e.g., `1.30.0`), and `helm unittest` for template logic before publishing.

Publish charts as **OCI artifacts** (`helm package` -> `helm push app-1.8.2.tgz oci://ghcr.io/acme/charts`), sign them with `cosign sign`, and pin exact chart versions in production pipelines rather than floating ranges (`^1.8.0`).

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Add `values.schema.json` to catch missing required keys or wrong types at render time.
- [ ] Always deploy with `--atomic --wait --timeout <duration> --history-max 10` in imperative CI.
- [ ] Add `checksum/config` and `checksum/secret` annotations to pod templates so config edits trigger rolling restarts.
- [ ] Omit `replicas` from `Deployment` templates whenever an `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` is active.
- [ ] Set `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded` on all hook `Job`s.
- [ ] Validate rendered YAML with `helm lint` and `kubeconform` in CI, and use `helm diff` before production upgrades.

interviewProblems.title: Helm Chart Releases
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Helm Chart Releases. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Helm packages Kubernetes manifests into versioned charts and tracks each deployment as an immutable, numbered release revision stored in-cluster for repeatable upgrades and rollbacks.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Kubernetes API Server applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Release Secrets (etcd).

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Release Secrets (etcd) experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Run `helm rollback <release> <last-deployed-rev>` (or `helm history` to verify the last `deployed` revision) rather than deleting the Secret manually.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Helm's value lies in atomic, revision-tracked releases (`--atomic --wait`) and parameterized reuse—treat rendered manifests as immutable build outputs and never mix manual `kubectl edit` into Helm-managed resources.
Avoid trap: Leaving `--history-max` at `10` or unlimited without checking Secret count, or conversely setting it to `0` (infinite) and bloating etcd.
Avoid trap: Hardcoding `replicas` inside `Deployment` when a `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` is enabled, causing Helm upgrades to reset autoscaled replica counts.
When to reach for it: Packaging third-party infrastructure (ingress-nginx, Prometheus, cert-manager, Kafka operators) distributed as OCI or HTTP Helm repositories.
When to reach for it: Standardizing internal microservice deployments across dozens of teams via a shared library or golden base chart.

putItTogether.title: Putting Helm Chart Releases Together
putItTogether.summary: Helm's value lies in atomic, revision-tracked releases (`--atomic --wait`) and parameterized reuse—treat rendered manifests as immutable build outputs and never mix manual `kubectl edit` into Helm-managed resources.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Helm Chart Releases before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: A `Job` annotated with `helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade` and `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded` runs the migration first. `helm upgrade payments oci://registry/payments --version 2.4.0 --atomic --wait --timeout 5m` pauses; if the new `Deployment` pods fail readiness within 5 minutes, Helm automatically rolls back to revision `v11`.
